mechanism_narrative: A lower federal funds rate relative to its 12-month average compresses the risk-free rate, reducing the discount rate for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below its 12-month average, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.2% (current rate is 4.1%) signals deteriorating labor market conditions, reducing consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When UNRATE rises above 4.2%, SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) indicates a broad-based weakening in aggregate demand, which triggers a negative S&P 500 return over the next 60 trading days as recession risks rise.
failure_condition: When both HOUST and RSAFS decline, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0), supply chain disruptions and reduced manufacturing output lead to higher inflation expectations and tighter monetary policy, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When INDPRO < 105.0, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A rising consumer spending trend (RSAFS) indicates strong aggregate demand, boosting corporate revenues and driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: When RSAFS rises, SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) above 2.5% signals accelerating inflation, prompting the Fed to tighten policy and reduce equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When CPIAUCSL > 250, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is negative.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both employment growth (PAYEMS) and a rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a weakening labor market, reducing consumer confidence and corporate hiring, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of high monetary policy rates (FEDFUNDS > 2.5%), the Fed's restrictive stance dampens economic growth and equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: When FEDFUNDS > 2.5%, SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases, or the Rank IC over 3 years is negative.
